text:
maya: Hey team, prospect (large fintech) asked for a clear breakdown of our incident response & breach notification timelines for their security review during the POC. they want a paragraph we can drop into their vendor risk form + a short bulleted process for technical buyers.

alex: I can draft. quick clarifiers: is this for Hosted API or Private deployment? obligations differ.

maya: Hosted first (POC uses hosted), but they asked what changes for Dedicated/Private. can we cover both briefly?

alex: Sure. For Hosted: we run our standard IR playbook. high-level timeline we give externally: initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of detection, preliminary customer notification within 72 hours if customer data is impacted or required by law, and ongoing updates at agreed cadences (e.g., 24–72h). final incident report + remediation plan within 30 days typically.

sam: +1. For Dedicated/Private: customers control the environment/network if deployed in their VPC or on-prem. We provide notification to the customer admin within 24 hours of detection and coordinate forensic access. Regulatory notifications remain the customer's responsibility unless the incident is caused by our control plane or by our managed services — we escalate per contract.

jordan: Can we add the standard internal steps? makes it easier for sales to explain.

alex: Internal IR steps (short): 1) Detect & Triage (T=0) — alerting + oncall engaged. 2) Contain — isolate affected nodes, rotate keys if needed. 3) Investigate/Forensics — preserve logs, collect artifacts. 4) Scope & Impact Assessment — data types, customers affected, timeframe. 5) Notify — internal, legal, customer ops per SLA. 6) Remediate & Validate — patch, config fixes, validation. 7) Postmortem & Report — timeline, root cause, mitigations.

maya: Perfect. can you also give a short customer-facing paragraph (2-3 sentences) we can paste into their vendor risk portal?

alex: Draft paragraph you can paste: "Redwood Inference maintains a documented incident response program. For our hosted service we acknowledge incidents within 24 hours, provide preliminary customer notification within 72 hours when customer data or regulatory obligations are implicated, and follow up with a detailed incident report and remediation plan. For Dedicated or Private deployments, we coordinate notifications and forensics with the customer's designated administrators; specific notification responsibilities depend on the contract and deployment model."

sam: add a short FAQ line: "Do you notify regulators?" answer: "We support customers with evidence and timelines; regulator notification is handled per contract and applicable law — we will assist if notification is required and cooperate with the customer's legal team."

jordan: sec-bot: IncidentBot: template files: `/ir/playbook/hosted-summary.md` and `/ir/templates/customer-notice.md` exist in our docs repo. link: https://internal.redwood/internals/ir (internal link).

maya: Great. one more — they asked about SLA credits or financial remedies if notification windows are missed. what's the standard reply?

alex: Generally we don't offer SLA credits tied to incident detection timelines; credits apply to uptime SLAs in Dedicated contracts. For enterprise deals we can add contract language around communication SLAs and escalation commitments — route to legal/enterprise sales for a term.

sam: Also flagged: they asked about evidence for SIG/CAIQ question on IR. we should point them at our CAIQ answers and attach the IR section table.

alex: I'll export the IR section from our CAIQ draft and attach it to the POC packet. includes runbooks, oncall rotation, engagement matrix, and encryption/key rotation notes.

maya: Thanks all — this is exactly what I need. I'll paste alex's paragraph into the vendor portal and attach the CAIQ IR excerpt + the short bulleted process. If legal needs to tweak contract language, i'll loop them in. :thumbsup:
